coaching.title: Easy 4mi Z2 Rolling
coaching.message: Easy 4 miles on rolling terrain, ~600 ft of climb. Keep HR strictly 138-150 bpm — conversational, controlled, no ego. You're 6 weeks out, so today is deliberate aerobic maintenance around a heavy travel day. Get out at first light before the El Salvador heat builds. Power-hike the steeper pitches and stay smooth on the descents to rehearse the up-down rhythm the Julian Alps will demand.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: It's a short easy run, so no in-run fueling needed — just top off with a few sips of water and a banana or a date beforehand if you feel empty. Because you're running in heat, add electrolytes (500-700mg sodium) to your bottle. After: rehydrate well and get 25-30g protein plus carbs within the hour, then keep eating normally through a travel-heavy day so you don't under-fuel while packing and driving.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: This session is easy by design, so recovery is mostly about the travel load, not the run. After you drive and land, get your legs elevated for 10-15 minutes, do light ankle and hip mobility to counter the sitting, and hydrate steadily. Protect sleep tonight despite the logistics — aerobic adaptations from an easy week are banked during rest, not the run itself.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Six weeks out, discipline looks like restraint. On a packed travel day it's tempting to skip or hammer — do neither. Nailing an easy run exactly as prescribed, in the heat, around chaos, is the reps that build an athlete who executes on race day in Kranjska Gora. Consistency under messy conditions is the real superpower. Trust the plan.
